svg.text: AI Models, Formats, GPU Compute & Inference Engines — Field Guide
Everything you need to understand what runs what, and why
① What kinds of AI models exist?
Trained to follow instructions and hold a conversation. You ask, it answers.
Examples in our stack: mistral:7b · phi3:mini · qwen2.5:3b
Thinks step-by-step before answering — shows its work. Slower but much
smarter on math, logic, coding. Examples: deepseek-r1:8b · deepseek-r1:14b
Not in our stack: Multimodal (text+images), Speech-to-text, Text-to-speech,
Diffusion (image generation). All different model architectures entirely.
② File formats — how model weights are stored on disk
③ ROCm — NOT a format. It's a GPU driver platform.
The model file (GGUF) stays the same. ROCm changes whether your
AMD GPU is used for the computation. Think: same MP4 video file,
ROCm vs CUDA — same idea, different GPU brand
CUDA = NVIDIA's GPU compute platform (GeForce, RTX, Tesla)
ROCm = AMD's GPU compute platform (Radeon, Instinct) — what we have
Both are invisible to the model. They are how the CPU talks to the GPU.
④ Inference Engines — what software runs the models
Local, easy, one model at a time
deepseek, mistral, phi3, qwen (needs HF weights)
deepseek, mistral, phi3, qwen (needs HF weights)
⑤ Models in our airgap stack
⑥ HuggingFace models (BERT-based — embedding + NER, not chat)
SQL model — same as sqlcoder2 in Ollama
KB-BERT is a BERT encoder — not generative, so Ollama/vLLM don't apply.
ONNX lets the Rust project (kb_bert_onnx) run it via onnxruntime-rs
without needing Python or PyTorch — fast, portable, CPU-friendly.
Flow: SafeTensors → export to ONNX → run via ONNX Runtime in Rust.
ROCm NOT needed — KB-BERT is tiny (124M params), CPU is fast enough.
— free for most use, restrictions on large-scale deployment
All models here publish their weights publicly. You can run them, fine-tune them. "Open-weight" ≠ fully open-source (training code/data may be closed).
